title: Width 512 -> 640 at depth 12
description: ASPECT_RATIO 40 -> 48, so model_dim goes 512 -> 640 (5 heads of 128) at unchanged DEPTH 12; nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE/flat: val_bpb 0.986993 vs baseline 0.986277, i.e. 0.0007 WORSE, inside the ~0.0009 noise floor. Numbers: params 71.3M -> 100.9M, FLOPs/token 3.46e8 -> 5.03e8 (+45%), total_tokens 331M -> 247.2M (-25%), num_steps 1886, steady-state MFU 38.5% -> 41.67%, peak VRAM 32.1 -> 40.7 GB. The wider model ran at higher MFU (wider matmuls are more efficient, as predicted) and still only broke even. Reading: the capacity axis is now saturated in BOTH directions at this 5-minute budget -- depth 12->14 projects to ~-0.001 and width 512->640 measured ~0.000, so at ~330M tokens the model is no longer the binding constraint; we have traded our way to roughly the compute-optimal shape and further parameters just buy fewer tokens. Remaining runs should go to non-capacity structure (MLP expansion ratio, window pattern, warmdown schedule) rather than another size step. Also worth noting: 45% more FLOPs/token cost only 25% of tokens because MFU rose, so the wall-clock price of size keeps falling -- but quality-per-token fell by exactly the offsetting amount.
